about.intro_content: Prof. Ming-Yuan Chen is Deputy Director of the Department of Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma and Director of the NPC Surgical Center at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC), Guangzhou. He pioneered minimally invasive surgical techniques for recurrent and refractory nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC).
about.detailed_content: Prof. Chen established a minimally invasive surgery treatment system for NPC and was the first internationally to apply minimally invasive surgery to stage I NPC, work that has been adopted into NPC clinical guidelines in the United Kingdom, the American College of Radiology, and the China Anti-Cancer Association. His surgical approach to recurrent NPC has been reported to improve overall survival by around 20% in his published outcomes data. He founded and chairs the Professional Committee of NPC of the Guangdong Provincial Anti-Cancer Association and was the first head-and-neck oncologist from mainland China invited to teach courses at the American Academy of Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery.

faq.section_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Prof. Ming-Yuan Chen

items.question: Does Prof. Ming-Yuan Chen accept international patients?
items.answer: CancerFax can coordinate medical report review and consultation support for international patients seeking an opinion related to nasopharyngeal carcinoma surgery at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, subject to hospital availability and case acceptance.

items.question: What is Prof. Chen's area of specialisation?
items.answer: Prof. Chen specialises in minimally invasive surgery for nasopharyngeal carcinoma, particularly recurrent, metastatic and necrotic disease that is difficult to treat with re-irradiation alone.

items.question: How can I request a consultation or second opinion?
items.answer: Submit your medical reports through CancerFax. The CancerFax team reviews the documents, prepares the case for submission, and coordinates next steps with SYSUCC's International Medical Center, subject to availability.

items.question: Is minimally invasive surgery suitable for recurrent nasopharyngeal carcinoma?
items.answer: For selected patients, minimally invasive surgery pioneered by Prof. Chen's team has been associated with improved survival compared with re-irradiation, though suitability depends on staging and case-by-case surgical assessment.

items.question: Has Prof. Chen's research shaped international treatment guidelines?
items.answer: Yes. His research on staging and minimally invasive surgery for recurrent and necrotic NPC has been incorporated into clinical guidelines in the United Kingdom, the American College of Radiology, and the China Anti-Cancer Association.
